# Cycle 0046: carried defects

The tasks of [Issue #87](https://github.com/laststance/codebook/issues/87) and of [the cycle record](0046-carried-defects-of-cycle-0045.md): every defect [Cycle 0045](0045-natural-request-and-carried-defects.md#next-action) left unfixed, copied in whole from the Issue as filed on 2026-10-05 against `main` `ae9c1f2`. Under the [cycle rule](../../AGENTS.md#cycle-rule-every-carried-defect-is-fixed-in-the-next-cycle) every row is a task, none is optional and none is carried again: a bug-fix cycle closes only when the **Closed** column names the fix and its test (the disabled-fix control recorded for a code change that changes behavior), or the evidence, on every row. A defect found while this cycle runs is added here with the next number and closed here.

Rows 1 to 8 are the defects Cycle 0045's native checks and local reviews named; rows 9 to 37 are PL-1 to PL-29 of the section "Pre-landing review of the delivery" of the Cycle 0045 record (its quoted lines and proposed fixes are there); rows 38 to 43 are its advice (PA-1 to PA-6); rows 44 and 45 are the documentation audit's items (DA-1 and DA-2); row 46 is record hygiene; rows 47 and later are defects found while this cycle runs (what the packages found beside their rows, and what the engineering review of rows 2, 9 and 16 to 18 found), added here under the cycle rule and closed here. Rows 2 and 9 are one mechanism (the owner's process start time recorded next to its pid in locks, takeover claims and markers). Rows 1, 5 and 6 name a choice within a stated bound, which the implementer makes and records with its evidence in the cycle record before building.

Totals: 514 rows (46 at filing on 2026-10-05, 468 found while the cycle runs and added under the cycle rule), CLOSED 493; 20 native-pending and 1 implementing.

| 9 | Cycle 0045, pre-landing review, PL-1 (Codex structured [P1], Claude adversarial) | `utils/isFromEarlierBoot.ts:19-22`, `utils/readBootIdentity.ts:27-29`, `utils/isRecordedOwnerGone.ts:25-26`: On Windows and macOS, where a boot is `{ startedAtMs: Date.now() - uptime }`, a wall-clock step of more than 60 s forward while a lock is held moves this boot's time past the recorded one, so `isRecordedOwnerGone` calls the live owner "from an earlier boot", `removeStaleStorageLock` removes the lock of a live window and two windows may write the saved data at once. The boot time is already left out for descriptors and profiles (`withoutBootTime`), not for locks and takeover claims. A table that is never closed (`<h2 id="a">A</h2><table><tr><td>cell</td></tr>`) is a boundary for the shell's end tags after the article: the shell's question form is then built empty, with its label, text area and button beside it, so Ask Codebook does nothing, and the rail lands inside the article.
